root_cause.text: In `pex_ep_event_pex_rst_deassert()`, the cleanup functions `pci_epc_deinit_notify()` and `dw_pcie_ep_cleanup()` (which internally access DBI registers) were invoked before `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)`, causing DBI register accesses while the controller core was still powered off, leading to a CBB timeout.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states the call chain: `pex_ep_event_pex_rst_deassert()` → `pci_epc_deinit_notify()` → ... → `dw_pcie_dbi_ro_wr_en()` (accesses DBI register 0x8bc) is called before `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)` powers on the core. The patch fixes this by moving the cleanup calls after `reset_control_deassert()`.

This cleanup function accesses DBI registers while the controller core is still in reset, leading to register access failure and timeout.
This application register write occurs while the core is powered off, potentially causing a timeout if the write triggers a DBI access or requires core power.
Similar to the previous line, this register access may indirectly depend on the core being powered and contributes to the vulnerability when executed out of order.
This reset deassert is placed after the cleanup functions; the late deassert causes the core to remain powered off during DBI accesses, enabling the vulnerability.
